title: Security dry-run notes — Morgan
content:
Quick context: running a 1st-pass dry-run of the SOC2 evidence collection for Security + Availability scope. Goal = find gaps in evidence names/locations and salvage easy wins before official control testing. These are my scratch observations; not an exhaustive list.

Top-level checklist (things I want to cover during 1st dry-run)
- Access controls: list of IAM groups, owner for each, screenshots of group membership (zoomed to show time stamp)
- Provisioning/deprovisioning: sample tickets (Jira), PRs for automation, time-to-decommission notes, one example of offboarding flow
- Change management: RFCs, code review policy evidence, change approvals for infra changes, canary rollback logs for one deploy
- Monitoring & alerting: sample pager duty incident (simulated), alerting runbook, metrics retention policy
- Data protection & encryption: KMS key usage log snippet, S3 bucket policy, DB encryption config screenshot
- Backups & DR: backup run log (last 90 days), restore test note (date, owner, outcome)
- Vendor mgmt: contracts + security questionnaire for any 3rd party with data access
- Incidents: incident timeline template filled for a past incident (redact PII), evidence of postmortem and remediation

Open questions I want to answer before handoff to auditor
- Which service accounts are considered ‘high-risk’? Need a crisp definition. (Morgan note: propose 'has read/write access to PII or writes to prod infra' as starting definition)
- Are there any long-lived personal SSH keys still in prod clusters? (Sven is checking)
- Retention windows: metrics vs logs vs audit logs — do we have a single table of retention policies? If not, create one.
- Are server images (AMIs/container base images) scanned with SCA/CVE feeds? Where are weekly reports?

Evidence naming convention (draft) — trying to avoid the chaos I found in the bucket
- evidence/<control-family>/<service>-<artifact-type>-YYYYMMDD-<owner-initials>.pdf
  examples: evidence/identity/okta-group-membership-20260215-mp.pdf
            evidence/change/infra-rfc-20260110-ar.pdf

Control mapping (quick sketch, map to TSC categories and local artifacts)
- TSC: Security — Control: Logical access management
  Local artifacts: Okta group exports, IAM role last-used logs, offboarding ticket template (JIRA-3421), one sample onboarding ticket
- TSC: Availability — Control: System monitoring and alerting
  Local artifacts: Monitoring retention policy doc, sample alert triggered (2026-01-20 pagerduty log), runbook for alert handling
- TSC: Security — Control: Change control
  Local artifacts: RFC from infra repo (PR #1287), approval thread in slack (#infra-changes), deployment canary logs
- TSC: Security — Control: Vendor/Third-party management
  Local artifacts: Vendor questionnaire (AcmeDB), contract redacted, vendor access spreadsheet (last updated 2026-01-05)

Dry-run findings (raw notes, untriaged)
- Found old S3 bucket policy named "legacy-exports" that sounds like it may contain logs. No owner listed. Flag for data-sensitivity review.
- One oncall rotation shows a gap (2-week window) where backup restore test wasn't performed. Need to schedule asap.
- Encryption evidence: DB encryption is on, but I couldn't find a KMS key rotation policy doc. Could be a gap.
- Some change approvals are done in PR comments, not in RFC doc. Need to capture governance note: acceptable? auditor will want consistent artifact.
- No consistent naming for evidence files; multiple teams use random folder names -> make MANDATORY evidence baseline.

Immediate actions (next 2 weeks)
- Create a central 'evidence index' doc with canonical paths and owners. (owner: Morgan)
- Ask SRE to run an inventory of service accounts and tag the 'high-risk' ones. (owner: Sven)
- Reach out to Legal for anonymized vendor contract copies or redaction guidance. (owner: Ava)
- Schedule 1 restore test and capture runbook and timestamped logs. (owner: Morgan, target: 2026-03-05)
- Draft evidence naming template and circulate to engineering leads. (owner: Morgan)

Evidence examples I will capture during the dry-run (practical list)
- OKTA export CSV (group members) + screenshot of Okta admin panel with timestamp
- IAM role last-used from cloud console (JSON truncated) + human-readable note of why role exists
- One deprovision ticket (JIRA-5582) showing steps completed and timestamped approvals
- PR + merge commit for infra change (PR 1287) showing reviewers and approval timestamp
- PagerDuty incident 2026-01-20 (summary + postmortem link)
- Backup job log for DB-analytics (2026-01-15) + restore test note 2026-03-05 (planned)

Notes to myself about auditor interactions
- Keep things simple, be ready to walk through one canonical example per control rather than 10 micro-examples.
- If auditor asks for historic evidence older than retention window, escalate to Legal/Records to confirm acceptability.
- For any gaps found, produce a remediation plan with owner + ETA; auditors expect a plan, not perfection.

Random thinking / friction points (brain dump)
- Too many teams store evidence in private team buckets. We need either a central evidence bucket or a short script to collect artifacts.
- Could automate 'evidence snapshot' once per sprint: a checklist in CI that grabs latest artifacts and zips with manifest. Low effort, high ROI.
- Consider adding an 'evidence tag' label in Jira so tickets that are evidence-ready are easier to filter.

Next meeting prep (for 2026-03-02 dry-run sync)
- Agenda: review central index draft, confirm high-risk service account list, sign up owners for missing artifacts, set dates for 2 restore tests
- Pre-reads: current evidence bucket list (I will share), infra RFC PR 1287, Okta group list export

Temporary notes / todo markers inside file (so I don't forget)
- TODO: Ask security tooling team for weekly SCA report exports (where are they stored?)
- TODO: Add short paragraph explaining retention differences between logs/metrics/audit-trails
- TODO: red-team notes? not part of SOC2 scope but useful for context

End of notes. Expect to trim and convert to a proper 'evidence index' doc after dry-run.

-- Morgan
